title: P0 HostedAPI streaming fragmentation diary and runbook draft
body:
Executive summary:

12/03/2026 03:14 UTC - a P0 was paged for an increase in client-facing streaming latency and a short wave of 5xxs on the hosted API streaming endpoint (/v1/streams). Impact lasted ~1h10m for a subset of customers; overall error rate peaked at 2.4% across streaming sessions and p99 tail latency for streaming chunks climbed from ~120ms to ~1.9s. Synchronous text-generation endpoints were largely unaffected.

Root-cause hypothesis (summary):
- Memory fragmentation in the C++ streaming buffer layer (custom slab allocator introduced in runtime v3.8.0) caused sporadic long allocation pauses and higher lock contention on the request fanout path.
- This was amplified by a concurrent autoscaler config (autoscaler-v2 rollout) that rebalanced replicas during the burst; some nodes received mixed non-streaming load which increased the allocator pressure and led to localized node-level degradation and transient 5xx responses.
- A low-probability interaction between the slab allocator and the garbage collection heuristics for the runtime's JS-based request router produced a rare condition where in-flight streaming sessions attempted to reserialize large buffered frames, which hit a path that triggered synchronous disk-backed spill to temp storage (cold-path) — increasing latency and connection resets.

Detection and alerting timeline (important timestamps):
- 03:10 UTC: Synthetic streaming canary p99 started drifting upward (noticed by synthetic dashboards).
- 03:12 UTC: On-call received alert: hosted-api-streaming-p99 > 800ms (pager).
- 03:14 UTC: Escalated to P0 after concurrent spike in 5xx errors on streaming shard cluster C.
- 03:18 UTC: On-call routed a fraction of traffic away from effected cluster to Dedicated pool as immediate mitigation.
- 03:27 UTC: Rolled back runtime v3.8.0 feature flag (slab allocator) on the most impacted pool; immediate drop in 5xx and reduction in p99 seen on those nodes within 90s.
- 03:38 UTC: Autoscaler rollout paused and autoscaler config rolled back to stable (v2.3.1).
- 04:20 UTC: Monitoring showed stabilized p99 ~150ms and 5xx rate <0.1% across streaming traffic.

Impact breakdown:
- Scope: ~12% of streaming capacity experienced high tail latency/5xx.
- Customers: Several enterprise customers observed degraded UX for streaming features (one support ticket flagged). No data loss detected; sessions recovered or were retried by clients.
- Duration: ~1h10m from detection to full remediation across all pools.

Immediate mitigations taken during incident: (ordered)
1) Traffic diversion: routed 25% of traffic from affected shard cluster to Dedicated pool with extra capacity. (owner: on-call)
2) Feature-flag rollback: disabled slab allocator via feature flag on impacted nodes. (owner: runtime-SRE)
3) Autoscaler pause and rollback to stable config. (owner: infra-oncall)
4) Increased streaming chunk soft-timeout from 3s->6s as a circuit-breaker to avoid immediate session resets during node recovery. (owner: streaming-service)

Evidence that supports root-cause:
- Memory allocation time-series showed spikes correlated to p99 latency windows on impacted nodes (heap/allocator metrics).
- Nodes with slab allocator disabled did not see the error wave during the same window.
- CPU profiles during the spike show long tails in allocator thread and increased mutex hold times in fanout path.
- No network anomalies, TLS failures, or disk saturation were observed.

Why previous mitigations didn't catch this earlier:
- Allocator fragmentation metric was added in the runtime but not instrumented into the streaming SLO dashboard; no pager rule existed for allocation-latency.
- Autoscaler rollout conditions were tuned to CPU-only signals and did not account for allocator-induced latency spikes.

Runbook draft (emergency steps for recurring event):
- Trigger: streaming-p99 > 600ms AND streaming-5xx-rate > 0.5% for > 2 minutes.
- Immediate steps (0-5 min):
  * Confirm via synthetic canary and cluster-level p99 metrics.
  * Increase routing weight to Dedicated pool by +30% for affected shard.
  * If feature-flag for slab allocator is enabled, flip to fallback allocator (FF: slab-allocator = off).
  * Pause in-flight autoscaler rollouts.
- Recovery steps (5-30 min):
  * Monitor node-level allocator metrics and mutex contention.
  * If 5xx persists, gracefully drain affected nodes and evict from rotation.
  * Enable extended chunk soft-timeout (config key streaming.chunk_soft_timeout) to reduce session resets.
- Post-recovery (30-120 min):
  * Keep diverted traffic for 1h while telemetry stabilizes.
  * Begin controlled canary for allocator re-enable on single node with traffic-limited canary.

Runbook TODOs (short-term):
- Add allocator fragmentation metric to streaming SLO dashboard and create pager rule. (owner: monitoring, due 2026-12-10)
- Add autoscaler signal for allocation-latency to avoid rebalancing during allocator pressure. (owner: infra, due 2026-12-17)
- Implement automated feature-flag flipback safeguards (prevent re-enable without canary). (owner: runtime, due 2026-12-13)

Longer-term engineering fixes and follow-ups:
- Runtime change: replace experimental slab allocator with upstream jemalloc + tune arena config (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7291). (owner: runtime-engineering, due 2027-01-14)
- Autoscaler: incorporate allocation latency and mutex hold-time signals into scaling decisions. (owner: platform-eng, due 2027-01-21)
- Streaming: remove disk-backed spill cold-path for normal in-flight frames; instead back-pressure to client with well-defined retry semantics. (owner: streaming-service, due 2027-01-07)
- Postmortem writeup and customer comms: prepare incident summary for CSM and support. (owner: eng-sre+cs, due 2026-12-07)

Notes to on-call and SREs (less formal):
- During the incident we observed a subtle signal: allocation timeouts on one node correlated with an increase in small allocation rates from non-streaming RPCs. This made the condition intermittent and noisy; synthetic-only alarms would have missed it.
- If you hit this again: rollback allocator flag first before draining nodes — that buys you ~60-120s of recovery on many nodes.
- The streaming soft-timeout increase is a blunt instrument; avoid raising it permanently without product sign-off.

Post-incident comms checklist (next 48 hours):
- Draft customer-facing note and share to #gcs-cs for review. (owner: Priya Shah)
- Internal postmortem to SRE execs with timeline + telemetry. (owner: Ravi Menon)
- Schedule a post-incident code review of runtime allocator PR. (owner: Marcus Li)

Appendix (links and quick artifacts):
- Telemetry graphs: streaming-p99, streaming-5xx-rate, allocator-alloc-latency, mutex-hold-time (dashboards linked in Jira SRE-2147).
- Incident Slack channel: #sre-incident-2026-12-03.
- Quick mitigations playbook: copy of this runbook will be added to Confluence once reviewed.

Open questions for follow-up meeting:
- What is the long-tail failure mode for the allocator when mixed workloads are present? Can we reproduce with a synthetic mix?
- Should Dedicated pool selection policy favor nodes with stable allocation metrics?
- Do product-level retry semantics for streaming need schema changes to better handle transient node-level serialization delays?

End of diary.

(Working draft — please add observations, telemetry snippets, and raw pprof captures here before we finalize the postmortem.)
